parts:
Well, you know how wide the error bars are, so can compute a position for the labels. For example:

# Sample data set
d <- structure(list(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(1, 2, 3), xwidth = c(1, 2, 3), lab = structure(c(1L, 3L, 2L), .Label = c("One", "Three", "Two"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("x", "y", "xwidth", "lab"), row.names = c(NA, -3L), class = "data.frame")

ggplot(d,aes(x,y))+geom_point()+geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin=x-xwidth,xmax=x+xwidth))+geom_text(aes(x=x+xwidth,label=lab),hjust=0)

Ben

parts:
Hi:

You can order the levels of x as follows:

d$x <- factor(d$x, levels = d$x)

I also think you could improve the positioning of the labels as follows (the change occurs in the geom_text() line):

forestplot2 <- function(d, ylab="Changes from the control %", xlab=""){
  require(ggplot2)
  print( ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, ymin=ylo, ymax=yhi, group=categ)) +
                theme_bw() +
                labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
                geom_point(size=3) + geom_errorbar(width=0) +
                geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) +
                geom_text(aes(y= yhi + 1, label=size), size=3) +
                coord_flip()

)
  #facet_wrap(~ categ,nrow=10, ncol=1, scales = "free_x")

invisible()
}

forestplot2(d)

Dennis
